items.summary: Police in Andhra Pradesh shot at and arrested Hemanth, the 21-year-old who attacked two Class 10 students, Gopika and Lakshmi, with a chainsaw inside a classroom in Anantapur district, on Sunday, November 1. Anantapur Superintendent of Police P Jagadeesh said six rounds were fired after Hemanth allegedly attacked police personnel attempting to arrest him near the Atmakur forest area. The accused, Hemanth, entered a classroom at a government school in Raptadu on Saturday, October 31, and attacked a 15-year-old student with a running chainsaw. He also injured another girl who tried to protect her classmate before fleeing the school. Speaking to reporters, Jagadeesh said police teams had been searching for Hemanth since the attack. Acting on information received on Sunday evening, two teams went to the Atmakur forest area, where they found him around 6.30 pm. According to the SP, Hemanth was intoxicated and resisted arrest. items.title: Uttarakhand SIR: 2,700+ names deleted in Gadarpur on objections filed by poll officers after the deadline
items.summary: “No eligible voter should be left out” has become the Election Commission’s refrain during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, repeated by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and in the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s press releases. In Uttarakhand’s Gadarpur constituency, the final roll tells a different story. According to Form 10 records published by the Uttarakhand Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), 10 Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) and the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO) filed 2,742 objections to delete voters on just two dates – September 18 (763) and September 28 (1,979). Both dates fell more than a month after the claims and objections period ended on August 13, with the second batch just logged five days before the final electoral roll was published. Rule 17 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, requires objections lodged after the prescribed period to be rejected. Electoral rules contain no provision for EROs or AEROs to file Form 7 themselves. items.title: Zoho’s Sridhar Vembu participates in RSS centenary march in Tamil Nadu
items.summary: Zoho co-founder and Chief Scientist Sridhar Vembu participated in a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) route march in Sankarankovil in Tamil Nadu’s Tenkasi district on November 1 alongside local BJP functionaries. The march was part of the second phase of RSS processions held across several districts to mark the organisation’s centenary year. Ananthan Ayyasamy, a BJP functionary from Tenkasi, shared photographs of the march on X and said Vembu had participated alongside the party’s district and town office-bearers. The November 1 procession was among RSS route marches held across Tamil Nadu following a Madras High Court order allowing the organisation to conduct them on October 25 and November 1, subject to conditions and local police requirements. The High Court on October 16 disposed of a petition after the state government told it that permission would be granted for the marches. Justice V Lakshminarayanan also directed the police to consider future applications in accordance with guidelines laid down in earlier cases and not delay decisions on them.
